is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.s. (M and S molecular forms) collected as larvae from rice paddies in M’Bé (page 2, 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for Vgsc L1014F (L995F), L1014S (L995S), and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) (page 3, 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 5: 'Concerning the kdr-w mutation (L1014F), the genotypes were distributed as follow among the M-form An. gambiae: 16 were resistant homozygotes (RR), 114 were heterozygotes (RS), and 93 were susceptible homozygotes (SS). The kdr-w frequency was 0.33. The three S-form specimens were respectively SS, RS and RR.' Table 2 gives allele frequencies and total sample size (226) for kdr-w (0.33), kdr-e (0.00), and ace-1R (0.00).

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae collected in May 2012 from rice paddies in M’Bé valley, Côte d'Ivoire, and reared to adulthood (page 2-3).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field research article evaluating insecticide resistance status and mechanisms.

sub_country_location.evidence: M’Bé valley (5.209963° W, 7.970241° N), 30 km north of Bouaké, Bandama department, Côte d'Ivoire (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field evaluation conducted by the study authors at the M'Bé field station.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype counts and frequencies are reported directly within the main text and Table 2.

assessment.summary: This study tested insecticide resistance and underlying resistance mechanisms in Anopheles gambiae s.s. (mostly M form / An. coluzzii) collected from M'Bé valley, Côte d'Ivoire, in May 2012. Genotyping of 226 mosquitoes identified Vgsc L1014F (16 RR, 114 RS, 93 SS in M-form; 1 RR, 1 RS, 1 SS in S-form; allelic frequency 0.33), while Vgsc L1014S and Ace-1 G119S were not detected (0.00).
